# Daily Dashboard V0.5.6

Windows can now lock the Dashboard main window to a chosen physical screen. Configure it under **Settings → General → Dedicated display**, then Save. Use **Use current screen** if your monitors have matching model names.

- Saves the Windows monitor device identity rather than a screen number, name or resolution.
- Starts the window hidden, validates the saved display and places it before showing it in borderless fullscreen.
- Guards Windows movement/show requests and rechecks topology, DPI/power changes and reconnects. Missing, ambiguous, mirrored or overlapping targets keep Dashboard hidden rather than moving it to the primary screen.
- The Windows tray menu offers Show on the selected screen, **Unlock display and show Dashboard**, and Quit. The executable also accepts `--unlock-display` for startup recovery.
- Settings writes preserve the other saved preferences, and recovery refreshes the frontend so stale forms do not restore an old binding.
- **macOS omits the monitor-lock control and Windows controller/tray implementation** and retains normal window/fullscreen behaviour.

[Setup and recovery guide](https://github.com/BananaAficionado/DailyDashboard/blob/Redesign/docs/dedicated-display.md).

This is desktop-window confinement. Keep the monitor enabled in the extended desktop; do not use Windows “Remove display from desktop”. Other apps, external browsers/Spotify/installers and Windows-owned dialogs retain their own placement rules.

## Verification

Production frontend build, frontend checks, 13 macOS native tests and full Windows cross-compilation pass. Browser checks cover all 456 widget/size/display combinations, Settings/focus/save interactions, plus monitor selection at all 19 documented resolutions/scaling configurations. Dedicated tests verify identity selection, save/reopen, failed validation, missing targets, recovery synchronization and macOS omission. Windows CI builds the installer and runs the Windows-native tests, including pre-placement guard and clone/overlap policy checks.

Physical Windows tests for your GPU/monitor/dock are still needed for unplug/replug, sleep/resume, display topology/DPI changes, move shortcuts and upgrade relaunch. Close the previous Dashboard before installing. The application identity and settings folder remain unchanged.
